raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With data parallelism, CPU KV offload sizes that fit `/dev/shm` one engine at a time but not all together make the engines fail after loading the model with `OSError: [Errno 14] Bad address`. Nothing in that error mentions `/dev/shm`. This PR warns about such sizes before any engine starts and turns the EFAULT into an error that names `/dev/shm`.

## Claims

- Before any engine starts, the launcher sums the offload budgets of the engines it is about to start on this host and, if `/dev/shm` cannot hold them, logs: *"Insufficient space in /dev/shm for CPU KV offload buffers of 8 data-parallel engines (32.0 GiB each, set by --kv-offloading-size): … MiB required, … MiB free. Increase /dev/shm (e.g. --shm-size or --ipc=host). Each engine rounds its region down to whole chunks, so each region may be up to one chunk smaller than its budget. The engines will still start; if /dev/shm runs out, the engine that cannot allocate its region reports it."* It is a warning, not a refusal, because that sum is an upper bound (see Details). Before this change, `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-size 32` against a 251.9 GiB `/dev/shm` loaded the model on all 8 engines, then 6 of them failed with "Bad address" and the server exited after 90 s, with nothing pointing at `/dev/shm`.
- When `/dev/shm` does run out while pre-faulting (budgets that really do not fit, other processes using it, or launch modes the check cannot see), the error says so: *"Ran out of /dev/shm while pre-faulting the CPU KV offload shared region (… GiB; /dev/shm has … GiB free of … GiB)…"*, chained from the original `OSError`.
- No warning where `/dev/shm` is not used: the CPU spec on ROCm and CPU keeps a private tensor per rank and is not checked (on XPU it maps the shared region, so it is checked). Config-only construction is not checked either; `VllmConfig` is untouched.

## Validation

The test and reproducer runs below used the nightly wheel of main `5c4b94be`, the commit merged into this branch, with the PR's files applied (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14), on a host whose GPUs were not available to the tests (they serve other work). A small local pytest plugin, not part of this PR, forced the CUDA platform and answered device-capability queries so that collection works without a device; the new tests patch the platform themselves and do not need it. GPU-dependent cases therefore fail there, identically with and without this PR; each suite was also run on unpatched `5c4b94be` and the failing test IDs compared.

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_shm_check.py`, `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py`: 103 passed. The new cases include one that drives the real `CoreEngineProcManager` with 8 engines and asserts that it warns and then goes on to spawn the engines, the review's rounding case (eight 32 GiB budgets against 255.5 GiB free: a warning, not a refusal), and EFAULT cases for the per-worker and sharded pre-fault that check the message, the chained `OSError`, that peers waiting at the barrier are released and that the file is removed. Against the previous revision's `shm_check.py`, the launch test, the rounding case and the three warning cases fail and the others pass. `test_startup_watch_processes.py` builds `CoreEngineProcManager` from a stub config, which now needs `kv_transfer_config=None`.
- `tests/v1/kv_offload`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector`, `test_offloading_connector.py`, `test_hisparse_connector.py` and `test_startup_watch_processes.py`: 1674 passed, 12 skipped; the 65 failures are the same test IDs as on unpatched main (mostly CUDA initialisation and device-count errors; 3 `offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` assertion failures fail identically on main). `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py`: 52 passed, the `shm_free_space` cases included; its 7 failures are multi-process tests that fail the same way on main.
- The offload config tests (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py`, `test_hma_auto_config.py`, `tests/test_config.py`) with a 64 MiB `/dev/shm` (Docker's default), mounted as a private tmpfs with `unshare -m`: 32 passed, as on main (the same 2 fail on both, "World size (4) is larger than the number of available GPUs").
- vLLM's pre-commit hooks pass on every changed file: ruff check and format, typos, mypy through `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` (Python 3.10 to 3.13), SPDX, lazy and forbidden imports, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`, test tethering.
- A GPU-free reproduction of the race: 4 processes each create a 1.5 GiB `SharedOffloadRegion` in a private 4 GiB tmpfs, 3 runs. On main, all 12 creations fail with "Bad address"; with this PR all 12 report "Ran out of /dev/shm while pre-faulting the CPU KV offload shared region …".
- End to end on this branch as merged with `5c4b94be`, 2× RTX 4090, Qwen3-8B, `--data-parallel-size 2 --kv-offloading-backend native`, each run with a private tmpfs on `/dev/shm`. A Qwen3-8B chunk is 2,359,296 B, so a budget of 8.000240325927734375 GiB per engine sits just under a chunk boundary and each region is 2,355,200 B smaller than its budget. Each 8 GiB region is split into 8 segments (#61680), so the last row also covers the segmented layout running out of `/dev/shm`:

  | `/dev/shm` | version | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | 40 GiB | this PR | healthy, no warning (166 s); the engines use 17,175,883,776 B of `/dev/shm` |
  | 16,382 MiB (that use + 2 MiB: both regions fit, the budgets do not) | previous revision | refused at launch, no model loaded (24 s) |
  | 16,382 MiB | this PR | warning, then healthy (66 s) |
  | 9,214 MiB (one engine's share + 1 GiB) | this PR | warning; both engines load the model, then each reports "Ran out of /dev/shm while pre-faulting the CPU KV offload shared region …", with the `Bad address` chained as its cause (60 s) |

- Before this PR, on the earlier base `642c18d6`: 8× RTX 4090, Qwen3-8B, `--data-parallel-size 8 --kv-offloading-size 32`, `/dev/shm` 251.9 GiB, on `main`: all 8 engines load the model, then 6 fail with `Bad address` and the server exits (90 s).

## Details

**Root cause.** Each region's creator checks `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm").free` against its own size and then calls `ftruncate`. On tmpfs, `ftruncate` creates a sparse file and reserves nothing, so N engines starting together all see the full tmpfs free and all pass. Pages are only claimed when `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` faults them in. On a full tmpfs, shmem returns `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS`, which `madvise` reports as `EFAULT`.

**Why the check is called from `CoreEngineProcManager`.** The check is `check_local_engines_offload_shm` in a new `vllm/v1/kv_offload/shm_check.py`; `CoreEngineProcManager` calls it once, before starting any engine. It reads the offload config and calls the existing `check_shm_free_space` with the engines' combined size, so `shared_offload_region.py` keeps only the `EFAULT` handling. The launcher is the one place that knows how many engines will share this host's `/dev/shm`. Inside an engine, a dense model's DP rank runs as an independent engine (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) with `data_parallel_size_local = 1`. A first version checked in `VllmConfig`, which had two problems. It refused configs on machines that never allocate anything, which broke the config tests above wherever `/dev/shm` is small. It also refused ROCm setups, where the CPU spec never uses `/dev/shm`. The launcher covers internal LB (MoE and dense), multi-node `--nnodes`, `--headless` with `--data-parallel-size-local`, and hybrid LB with `--data-parallel-start-rank`.

**Which specs are checked.** The check asks the spec class (`_uses_shared_region`, now a classmethod): true for `CPUOffloadingSpec` on CUDA and XPU and for `TieringOffloadingSpec` everywhere. A custom spec that does not subclass these is skipped. With `spec_module_path`, the front-end therefore imports that module once. An out-of-tree subclass that overrides the (private) `_uses_shared_region` as an instance method would now fail at launch with a `TypeError`.

**Free space, like every other `/dev/shm` allocation.** At launch the engines have allocated nothing, so the free space is what they will share. The comparison is `check_shm_free_space` itself, so it uses the same message as a single engine's own check; its `RuntimeError` is caught and logged, and the cgroup headroom it would have logged next is logged too. Anything that fills `/dev/shm` after the check is left to the per-region check and, failing that, to the clearer `EFAULT` message.

**Why a warning, not a refusal.** The sum is of the configured budgets, but `CPUOffloadingSpec` allocates `num_chunks = cpu_bytes_to_use // aligned_kv_bytes_per_chunk`, so each region can be up to one chunk smaller than its budget, and the chunk size depends on the KV cache spec, which does not exist until an engine is up. Refusing on the sum would reject configurations whose regions fit (eight 32 GiB budgets with 320 MiB chunks allocate 255 GiB, which a refusal would reject with 255.5 GiB free). The cost is that a configuration that is far over now loads the model on every engine before it fails, instead of failing in seconds; it still fails with a message that names `/dev/shm`.

**Rejected: reserving with `posix_fallocate`.** It would make the check and the claim atomic, but on tmpfs it allocates the pages under the caller's memory policy. Measured: a file fallocated from NUMA node 3 and then populated from node 5 had 512 of 512 sampled pages on node 3. Every TP rank's slots would land on the creator's node instead of each rank's own.

**Related.** Recent changes to the same region: #59546 splits it across several `/dev/shm` files, #59545 and #60869 spread the pre-fault across workers (`populate_shard`), and #59544 pins only each worker's own slots. None changes how much `/dev/shm` the region needs, when that is checked, or what a full tmpfs reports; the `EFAULT` translation here covers every pre-fault path (per worker, whole region, sharded). Open: #59547 gives each rank its own region and file, and its review notes the same under-detection when several ranks create regions at once; the launcher's per-engine total stays correct under that design. #53073 reworks ownership and cleanup in the same constructor and #61680 (merged) added segments to the HiSparse pool at the call this PR edits; main is merged into this branch with both kept. #59430 (closed unmerged) had parallelised the pre-fault with a thread pool.

**Limitations.**
- Launch modes where each process starts one engine are not covered by the check, only by the error message: external LB (`--data-parallel-rank`), `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb` (its children run with a local size of 1), offline DP with one `LLM` per rank, and independent single-engine servers sharing a host. The Ray backend (`CoreEngineActorManager`) is not checked either.
- Only an `OffloadingConnector` configured directly is checked: one nested in a `MultiConnector` (e.g. with a PD connector) and HiSparse's shared host pool are not added to the sum, though both get the clearer `EFAULT` message.
- After an `EFAULT` in a region without a barrier (the tiering scheduler's), the partly faulted file stays in `/dev/shm`, as it does today, so lowering the size may not be enough until it is removed (#51730, #54619 address cleanup).
- On kernels older than 5.14, there is no `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`, and the per-page fallback hits a SIGBUS that cannot be translated.
- Under a memory-cgroup limit, the failure is `ENOMEM` or the OOM killer, not `EFAULT`.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.

I feel like the more appropriate location to add such check would be in [check_shm_free_space](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c5b32e6b6d69b2518e9c6b0a0e9d5c2d27ff64b/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py#L231) instead.

Thanks for the review! Makes sense. I've moved the check out of shared_offload_region.py, so that file now only has the EFAULT handling. The check itself now lives in vllm/v1/kv_offload/shm_check.py (new file), and CoreEngineProcManager calls it once before it starts the engines. It adds up the offload buffers of all the engines on the host and passes that total to check_shm_free_space, so the actual comparison, the error message and the cgroup logging all come from check_shm_free_space. As a side effect it now compares against free space instead of total, like the other /dev/shm allocations do.

I didn't put the logic inside check_shm_free_space itself like you suggested because it's a generic helper that just gets a byte count. It's also used by ShmRingBuffer, ShmTensorArena and Engram, and it has no way of knowing how many engines will share the host. The engines can't tell either: a dense model's DP rank gets reconfigured to data_parallel_size_local = 1, so each one only sees its own buffer. And since ftruncate on tmpfs doesn't reserve anything, they all see the same free space and all pass. The launcher is the only place that knows the engine count before anything gets allocated, so that's where the total is computed. I kept the offload-specific parts (the connector, cpu_bytes_to_use, and which specs actually use /dev/shm) in the kv_offload package, so the launcher only gets one import and one call.

I also tried doing it in VllmConfig early on, but that refused configs on machines that never allocate anything (the config tests fail with Docker's 64 MiB /dev/shm), and it refused ROCm setups where the CPU spec doesn't use /dev/shm at all.

Hey @mushroomcarbon,
Thank you for the PR!

Generally we prefer to keep shared_offload_region.py clean of such config related checks.
I feel like the more appropriate location to add such check would be in [check_shm_free_space](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c5b32e6b6d69b2518e9c6b0a0e9d5c2d27ff64b/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py#L231) instead.
Moving the check out of `shared_offload_region.py` addresses my earlier concern. There’s still a sizing mismatch that can reject configurations whose regions fit. Please address that before merging.

Can we avoid hard-failing on the unrounded budget here? `CPUOffloadingSpec` rounds down to whole chunks. For example, eight 32 GiB budgets with 320 MiB chunks allocate 255 GiB total, but this rejects them with 255.5 GiB free. We should check the actual allocation size, or make this estimate advisory until that size is known.

Thank you for the review once more, and good catch. I went with making it advisory. The launcher can’t really know the actual allocation size, since the chunk size depends on the KV cache spec, which only exists once the engines are up. So now it just logs a warning when the total doesn’t fit and lets the engines start, same as how check_shm_free_space already treats cgroup headroom. If /dev/shm actually does run out, the engine that can’t get its region still fails with the clearer /dev/shm error instead of “Bad address”.

I added a test with your example (8 x 32 GiB with 255.5 GiB free now warns instead of refusing) and checked it end to end on a couple of 4090s. I also merged main to fix the conflict with #61680 and updated the description.

## Details

**Root cause.** Each region's creator checks `shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm").free` against its own size and then calls `ftruncate`. On tmpfs, `ftruncate` creates a sparse file and reserves nothing, so N engines starting together all see the full tmpfs free and all pass. Pages are only claimed when `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` faults them in. On a full tmpfs, shmem returns `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS`, which `madvise` reports as `EFAULT`.

**Why the check is called from `CoreEngineProcManager`.** The check is `check_local_engines_offload_shm` in a new `vllm/v1/kv_offload/shm_check.py`; `CoreEngineProcManager` calls it once, before starting any engine. It reads the offload config and calls the existing `check_shm_free_space` with the engines' combined size, so `shared_offload_region.py` keeps only the `EFAULT` handling. The launcher is the one place that knows how many engines will share this host's `/dev/shm`. Inside an engine, a dense model's DP rank runs as an independent engine (`reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank`) with `data_parallel_size_local = 1`. A first version checked in `VllmConfig`, which had two problems. It refused configs on machines that never allocate anything, which broke the config tests above wherever `/dev/shm` is small. It also refused ROCm setups, where the CPU spec never uses `/dev/shm`. The launcher covers internal LB (MoE and dense), multi-node `--nnodes`, `--headless` with `--data-parallel-size-local`, and hybrid LB with `--data-parallel-start-rank`.

**Which specs are checked.** The check asks the spec class (`_uses_shared_region`, now a classmethod): true for `CPUOffloadingSpec` on CUDA and XPU and for `TieringOffloadingSpec` everywhere. A custom spec that does not subclass these is skipped. With `spec_module_path`, the front-end therefore imports that module once. An out-of-tree subclass that overrides the (private) `_uses_shared_region` as an instance method would now fail at launch with a `TypeError`.

**Free space, like every other `/dev/shm` allocation.** At launch the engines have allocated nothing, so the free space is what they will share. The comparison is `check_shm_free_space` itself, so it uses the same message as a single engine's own check; its `RuntimeError` is caught and logged, and the cgroup headroom it would have logged next is logged too. Anything that fills `/dev/shm` after the check is left to the per-region check and, failing that, to the clearer `EFAULT` message.

**Why a warning, not a refusal.** The sum is of the configured budgets, but `CPUOffloadingSpec` allocates `num_chunks = cpu_bytes_to_use // aligned_kv_bytes_per_chunk`, so each region can be up to one chunk smaller than its budget, and the chunk size depends on the KV cache spec, which does not exist until an engine is up. Refusing on the sum would reject configurations whose regions fit (eight 32 GiB budgets with 320 MiB chunks allocate 255 GiB, which a refusal would reject with 255.5 GiB free). The cost is that a configuration that is far over now loads the model on every engine before it fails, instead of failing in seconds; it still fails with a message that names `/dev/shm`.

**Rejected: reserving with `posix_fallocate`.** It would make the check and the claim atomic, but on tmpfs it allocates the pages under the caller's memory policy. Measured: a file fallocated from NUMA node 3 and then populated from node 5 had 512 of 512 sampled pages on node 3. Every TP rank's slots would land on the creator's node instead of each rank's own.

**Related.** Recent changes to the same region: #59546 splits it across several `/dev/shm` files, #59545 and #60869 spread the pre-fault across workers (`populate_shard`), and #59544 pins only each worker's own slots. None changes how much `/dev/shm` the region needs, when that is checked, or what a full tmpfs reports; the `EFAULT` translation here covers every pre-fault path (per worker, whole region, sharded). Open: #59547 gives each rank its own region and file, and its review notes the same under-detection when several ranks create regions at once; the launcher's per-engine total stays correct under that design. #53073 reworks ownership and cleanup in the same constructor and #61680 (merged) added segments to the HiSparse pool at the call this PR edits; main is merged into this branch with both kept. #59430 (closed unmerged) had parallelised the pre-fault with a thread pool.

**Limitations.**
- Launch modes where each process starts one engine are not covered by the check, only by the error message: external LB (`--data-parallel-rank`), `--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb` (its children run with a local size of 1), offline DP with one `LLM` per rank, and independent single-engine servers sharing a host. The Ray backend (`CoreEngineActorManager`) is not checked either.
- Only an `OffloadingConnector` configured directly is checked: one nested in a `MultiConnector` (e.g. with a PD connector) and HiSparse's shared host pool are not added to the sum, though both get the clearer `EFAULT` message.
- After an `EFAULT` in a region without a barrier (the tiering scheduler's), the partly faulted file stays in `/dev/shm`, as it does today, so lowering the size may not be enough until it is removed (#51730, #54619 address cleanup).
- On kernels older than 5.14, there is no `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`, and the per-page fallback hits a SIGBUS that cannot be translated.
- Under a memory-cgroup limit, the failure is `ENOMEM` or the OOM killer, not `EFAULT`.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# /dev/shm exhaustion while pre-faulting
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("named", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("populate_shard", [None, (0, 2)])
+def test_populate_efault_reports_shm_exhaustion(
+    iid, monkeypatch, populate_shard, named
+):
+    """A full tmpfs makes MADV_POPULATE_WRITE fail with EFAULT ("Bad
+    address"); the region must say that /dev/shm ran out instead, naming the
+    allocation and the option that sizes it, and still release its peers."""
+    calls = 0
+
+    def efault_after_probe(*_):
+        nonlocal calls
+        calls += 1
+        if calls > 1:
+            raise OSError(errno.EFAULT, "Bad address")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(region_module, "_madvise_populate_write", efault_after_probe)
+    name, option = (
+        ("test pool", "--test-pool-size")
+        if named
+        else (
+            "CPU KV offload shared region",
+            "--kv-offloading-size",
+        )
+    )
+    kwargs = {"shm_allocation_name": name, "shm_size_option": option} if named else {}
+    barrier = MagicMock()
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Ran out of /dev/shm") as exc:
+        SharedOffloadRegion(
+            engine_id=iid,
+            num_chunks=4,
+            rank=0,
+            kv_bytes_per_chunk=PAGE_SIZE,
+            cpu_page_size=PAGE_SIZE,
+            barrier=barrier,
+            populate_shard=populate_shard,
+            **kwargs,
+        )
+    assert f"the {name}" in str(exc.value)
+    assert f"Lower {option}" in str(exc.value)
+    assert isinstance(exc.value.__cause__, OSError)
+    assert calls == 2  # the probe, then the first real pre-fault
+    assert barrier.call_count == (1 if populate_shard is None else 2)
+    assert not os.path.exists(f"/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{iid}.mmap")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""/dev/shm capacity for the CPU KV offload buffers of data-parallel engines
+that share one host."""
+
+import logging
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import ANY, MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.config import KVTransferConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed.device_communicators import shm_broadcast
+from vllm.utils import cpu_resource_utils
+from vllm.v1.engine import utils as engine_utils
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload import shm_check
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.shm_check import check_local_engines_offload_shm
+
+GiB = 1 << 30
+
+
+def _fake_shm(monkeypatch, free: int) -> None:
+    usage = shm_broadcast.shutil.disk_usage(shm_broadcast.SHM_PATH)._replace(
+        total=free, free=free
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(shm_broadcast.shutil, "disk_usage", lambda _: usage)
+
+
+def _fake_platform(monkeypatch, kind: str) -> None:
+    from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu import spec as cpu_spec_module
+
+    platform = SimpleNamespace(
+        is_cuda_alike=lambda: kind in ("cuda", "rocm"),
+        is_rocm=lambda: kind == "rocm",
+        is_xpu=lambda: kind == "xpu",
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cpu_spec_module, "current_platform", platform)
+
+
+def _offload_vllm_config(spec_name: str = "CPUOffloadingSpec", connector=None):
+    return VllmConfig(
+        kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(
+            kv_connector=connector or "OffloadingConnector",
+            kv_role="kv_both",
+            kv_connector_extra_config={
+                "spec_name": spec_name,
+                "cpu_bytes_to_use": 32 * GiB,
+            },
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def _stub_cgroup(monkeypatch) -> MagicMock:
+    """Stub the cgroup preflight, whose reading of the host's own cgroup files
+    is not what these tests are about, and return the stub the launcher's
+    warning path calls."""
+    cgroup = MagicMock()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cpu_resource_utils, "check_cgroup_memory_available", cgroup)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(shm_broadcast, "check_cgroup_memory_available", MagicMock())
+    return cgroup
+
+
+def _warnings(caplog) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        r.getMessage()
+        for r in caplog.records
+        if r.name == shm_check.__name__ and r.levelno == logging.WARNING
+    ]
+
+
+def _warning(caplog) -> str:
+    warnings = _warnings(caplog)
+    assert len(warnings) == 1, warnings
+    return warnings[0]
+
+
+class _Spawned(Exception):
+    """Raised in place of starting the engine processes."""
+
+
+def test_engine_launch_warns_then_starts_the_engines(monkeypatch, caplog_vllm):
+    """The warning must be emitted where the local engines are started, before
+    any of them runs: inside an engine, a dense model's data-parallel rank sees
+    only itself. It must not stop the launch, because the size compared here is
+    an upper bound (see check_local_engines_offload_shm)."""
+    _fake_shm(monkeypatch, 252 * GiB)
+    _fake_platform(monkeypatch, "cuda")
+    _stub_cgroup(monkeypatch)
+
+    def spawned():
+        raise _Spawned
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(engine_utils, "get_mp_context", spawned)
+    with pytest.raises(_Spawned):
+        engine_utils.CoreEngineProcManager(
+            local_engine_count=8,
+            start_index=0,
+            local_start_index=0,
+            vllm_config=_offload_vllm_config(),
+            local_client=True,
+            handshake_address="ipc:///unused",
+            executor_class=MagicMock(),
+            log_stats=False,
+        )
+    message = _warning(caplog_vllm)
+    assert "offload buffers of 8 data-parallel engines" in message
+    assert "still start" in message
+
+
+def test_budget_that_rounds_down_to_fit_is_not_refused(monkeypatch, caplog_vllm):
+    """CPUOffloadingSpec allocates num_chunks = cpu_bytes_to_use //
+    aligned_kv_bytes_per_chunk, so a region is at most its budget: eight 32 GiB
+    budgets with 320 MiB chunks allocate 255 GiB, which fits here. The launcher
+    cannot know the chunk size, so it may warn, but it must not refuse."""
+    _fake_shm(monkeypatch, 255 * GiB + GiB // 2)
+    _fake_platform(monkeypatch, "cuda")
+    _stub_cgroup(monkeypatch)
+
+    check_local_engines_offload_shm(_offload_vllm_config(), 8)
+
+    # 8 x 32 GiB budgeted against 255.5 GiB free: a warning, not a refusal.
+    message = _warning(caplog_vllm)
+    assert "262144 MiB required, 261632 MiB free" in message
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "spec_name,platform,connector,engines,warns",
+    [
+        # 8 x 32 GiB overfills 252 GiB of free /dev/shm; 7 x 32 GiB fits.
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "cuda", None, 8, True),
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "cuda", None, 7, False),
+        # One engine is left to its own free-space check.
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "cuda", None, 1, False),
+        # The CPU spec keeps a private tensor per rank on ROCm, not /dev/shm.
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "rocm", None, 8, False),
+        # XPU maps the shared region too.
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "xpu", None, 8, True),
+        # Tiering uses the shared region on every platform.
+        ("TieringOffloadingSpec", "rocm", None, 8, True),
+        ("CPUOffloadingSpec", "cuda", "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector", 8, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_local_engines_shm_check_scope(
+    monkeypatch, caplog_vllm, spec_name, platform, connector, engines, warns
+):
+    _fake_shm(monkeypatch, 252 * GiB)
+    _fake_platform(monkeypatch, platform)
+    cgroup = _stub_cgroup(monkeypatch)
+
+    check_local_engines_offload_shm(_offload_vllm_config(spec_name, connector), engines)
+
+    if warns:
+        assert "Insufficient space in /dev/shm" in _warning(caplog_vllm)
+        # check_shm_free_space raises before its own cgroup preflight, so the
+        # warning path runs it for the same total.
+        cgroup.assert_called_once_with(engines * 32 * GiB, ANY)
+    else:
+        assert _warnings(caplog_vllm) == []
+        cgroup.assert_not_called()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_local_engines_offload_shm(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig", local_engine_count: int
+) -> None:
+    """Warn when the CPU KV offload buffers of the engines about to start on
+    this host may not fit in /dev/shm together.
+
+    Each engine checks free space only for its own region, and ftruncate
+    reserves nothing, so engines started together all see the same free space
+    and can exhaust it while pre-faulting. A single engine is left to its own
+    check, and specs that keep their buffer out of /dev/shm are skipped.
+
+    The size this can compute is an upper bound: it is the configured budget,
+    while CPUOffloadingSpec rounds each engine's region down to whole chunks,
+    and the chunk size is not known until an engine has its KV cache spec. So
+    this logs a warning instead of refusing the launch, like the cgroup
+    preflight that check_shm_free_space runs.
+    """
+    if local_engine_count < 2:
+        return
+    ktc = vllm_config.kv_transfer_config
+    if ktc is None or ktc.kv_connector != "OffloadingConnector":
+        return
+    extra_config = ktc.kv_connector_extra_config
+    cpu_bytes = int(extra_config.get("cpu_bytes_to_use") or 0)
+    if not cpu_bytes:
+        return
+
+    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.shm_broadcast import (
+        check_shm_free_space,

inline_comments.body: Can we avoid hard-failing on the unrounded budget here? `CPUOffloadingSpec` rounds down to whole chunks. For example, eight 32 GiB budgets with 320 MiB chunks allocate 255 GiB total, but this rejects them with 255.5 GiB free. We should check the actual allocation size, or make this estimate advisory until that size is known.

Thank you for the review once more, and good catch. I went with making it advisory. The launcher can’t really know the actual allocation size, since the chunk size depends on the KV cache spec, which only exists once the engines are up. So now it just logs a warning when the total doesn’t fit and lets the engines start, same as how check_shm_free_space already treats cgroup headroom. If /dev/shm actually does run out, the engine that can’t get its region still fails with the clearer /dev/shm error instead of “Bad address”.

I added a test with your example (8 x 32 GiB with 255.5 GiB free now warns instead of refusing) and checked it end to end on a couple of 4090s. I also merged main to fix the conflict with #61680 and updated the description.

> Generally we prefer to keep shared_offload_region.py clean of such config related checks. I feel like the more appropriate location to add such check would be in [check_shm_free_space](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c5b32e6b6d69b2518e9c6b0a0e9d5c2d27ff64b/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py#L231) instead.

Thanks for the review! Makes sense. I've moved the check out of shared_offload_region.py, so that file now only has the EFAULT handling. The check itself now lives in vllm/v1/kv_offload/shm_check.py (new file), and CoreEngineProcManager calls it once before it starts the engines. It adds up the offload buffers of all the engines on the host and passes that total to check_shm_free_space, so the actual comparison, the error message and the cgroup logging all come from check_shm_free_space. As a side effect it now compares against free space instead of total, like the other /dev/shm allocations do.

I didn't put the logic inside check_shm_free_space itself like you suggested because it's a generic helper that just gets a byte count. It's also used by ShmRingBuffer, ShmTensorArena and Engram, and it has no way of knowing how many engines will share the host. The engines can't tell either: a dense model's DP rank gets reconfigured to data_parallel_size_local = 1, so each one only sees its own buffer. And since ftruncate on tmpfs doesn't reserve anything, they all see the same free space and all pass. The launcher is the only place that knows the engine count before anything gets allocated, so that's where the total is computed. I kept the offload-specific parts (the connector, cpu_bytes_to_use, and which specs actually use /dev/shm) in the kv_offload package, so the launcher only gets one import and one call.

I also tried doing it in VllmConfig early on, but that refused configs on machines that never allocate anything (the config tests fail with Docker's 64 MiB /dev/shm), and it refused ROCm setups where the CPU spec doesn't use /dev/shm at all.
